title: Deciding whether an exact MMS allocation exists
area: Algorithmic game theory, mechanism design and fair division
formal: What is the computational complexity of deciding whether a finite instance of indivisible goods with binary-encoded nonnegative additive valuations admits a complete allocation giving each agent at least her n-way maximin share?
context:
The number n of agents is part of the input. This is an existence decision problem for a given instance, not the optimal universally guaranteed approximation factor.

This question was found through Wikipedia and compared individually with the existing candidate and archived records. The linked literature provides definitions and background; this import is not a completed research-card review.
why: Distinguishes the complexity of attaining a fairness guarantee from the difficulty of evaluating each agent's benchmark.
